mechanism.bytes: rev0 anchor = FF 1F (call far [bx]) written by stosw AX=1FFFh at ES:DI=0FFBh:xxA2 (arena in-page 52h, residue 2 mod 4); while dwelling, DI=xxA3, DS=private 2 KiB segment. A MOVSW-family trail is laid in 4-byte blocks [A5, IPhi, CSlo, CShi] with A5 at residue 3. Moving downward, the first block that reaches us covers anchor+1..anchor+4, so the anchor becomes FF A5 IPhi CSlo = jmp near [di+(CSlo:IPhi)]. On our next turn that read goes to DS=private at EA=DI+d16, which is outside the 2 KiB region, and the engine raises a memory exception. A MOVSB trail puts A4 on the anchor instead, which only triggers our own rebuild.
examples: sthreat-movsw_cgx123123 r7968 CAND2 0FFB:F8A2 bytes ff a5 f7 00 10 a5 f7 00 (A5 written by A_IND_cgx123123 in r7967), memory exception
sthreat-movsw_Baltika9 r198 CAND2 0FFB:C4A2 bytes ff a5 c3 f6 0f a5 c3 f6 (Baltika92 r197), memory exception
s2025-3 r266 CAND2 0FFB:C4A2 bytes ff a5 c1 06 10 a5 (A_OHS_TrojanByte r265)
mechanism.traceCounts: 161 CAND deaths in 160 battles (4 2025 + 4 MOVSW-threat cohorts). 80 were anchor FF A5 (first MOVSW push) and 2 were anchor ?? A5 (second push), all memory exceptions. Writers of the A5 byte: Y_TOM_Code_Killer 31, A_IND_cgx123123 22, A_WAN_Baltika9 13, A_OHS_TrojanByte 10, A_WHS_K0F1M_AL_T1L1M 5, zom20b 1. The other 79 deaths were not at the anchor or had a different anchor corruption.

recommendation: Do not promote B051-movsw43. The MOVSW anchor kill is verified and is the largest single cause of death in this trace. No byte-level fix looks feasible: the jmp [di+d16] reads outside the private 2 KiB or into arbitrary data, and the A5 residue is tied to the trigger byte. Switching family moves the weakness onto the V6/Chimera MOVSB crowd, which costs more. Add B051_V6MOVSW53 to the threat library as a cheap anti-rev0 counter.
